jurisdiction.name: Tuvalu
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Tuvalu has no national AI law, strategy or official AI guidance. AI appears only in donor-supported projects such as AI-based weather forecasting and a national digital twin. Its digital agenda runs through the 2023 National ICT Policy and the Digital Nation initiative.
lead_institutions: Department of Information and Communications Technology
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 13 October 2026, but the official legislation portal, the ICT department's, the government portal's and Parliament's websites could not be accessed, so no official document could be read. Tuvalu is marked for a later retry. The National ICT Policy and pending cybercrime and electronic transactions bills are tracked as leads.

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-13, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. tuvalu-legislation.tv and PacLII HTTP 403 (curl and WebFetch); ict.gov.tv 503/reset; gov.tv and parliament.gov.tv proxy 502. Web search only (14 queries). No data protection authority. 'Data Protection and Privacy Act 2020' secondary sources only. Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: Searched, nothing found: no AI law, no data protection law and no AI provisions identified; tuvalu-legislation.tv and PacLII returned 403 to curl and WebFetch, so the portal's own search could not be run (web searches found no AI legislation; cybercrime and electronic transactions bills reported pending, held as leads). Parliament site (parliament.gov.tv) unreachable.; Government: Searched, nothing found: no national AI strategy or public-sector AI guidance. Te Kete National Strategy for Sustainable Development 2021-2030 shows no AI content in search results; National ICT Policy (2023) held as lead (text not located). Department of ICT site (ict.gov.tv) unreachable (503 / connection reset); gov.tv portal unreachable (502).; Ministries: Searched, nothing found: no education, health, justice or other ministry AI documents found by web search; ministry sites not reachable.; Regulators: Searched, nothing found: Tuvalu has no data protection authority; no AI documents found for the telecom/ICT regulator function, financial authorities or cyber bodies.. Not reached: tuvalu-legislation.tv own search (HTTP 403 to curl and WebFetch); ict.gov.tv (503 / connection reset); gov.tv and parliament.gov.tv (proxy 502). Could not verify: National ICT Policy (2023) content and date; reported Data Protection and Privacy Act 2020 (secondary sources only); status of Cybercrime and Electronic Transactions Bills. binding-law, strategy, government-governance, ethics, risk-assurance, public-sector, procurement, cyber-security, data-privacy, transparency, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, sectoral, generative-ai, drafts, international, historical: no material found.

leads.title: National ICT Policy (Tuvalu, reported approved 5 October 2023)
leads.english_title: National Information and Communications Technology Policy
leads.issuing_authority: Government of Tuvalu (Department of ICT, Ministry of Transport, Energy, Communications and Innovation)
leads.note: Known only from secondary trackers (reported approval 5 October 2023; seven strategic focuses incl. connectivity, digital government and cybersecurity). Official text not located: Department of ICT site (ict.gov.tv) and Tuvalu legislation portal unreachable from this environment. Check whether it contains an AI or emerging-technology pillar before recording (scope test).

leads.title: Cybercrime Bill (Tuvalu, pending)
leads.issuing_authority: Government of Tuvalu / Parliament of Tuvalu
leads.note: Reported by secondary sources as drafted and pending (no dedicated cybercrime statute enacted); no official text located. Check for any AI/deepfake provisions once published on tuvalu-legislation.tv.

leads.title: Electronic Transactions Bill (Tuvalu)
leads.note: Reported in 2023 as being prepared after a 2020 gap analysis covering electronic transactions, data protection, consumer protection and cybercrime; status unknown; no official text located. Unverified secondary reports also mention a 'Data Protection and Privacy Act 2020' that could not be confirmed on any official source.

leads.title: National Security Policy (Tuvalu, in development)
leads.note: Reported in development after Cabinet endorsement in September 2025, covering cyber security among other areas; no official text located and no indication of AI content.
